“Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace.”

Literature-consistent read: The 50 bp rate cut, paired with “greater confidence” that inflation is moving toward 2% and “balanced” risks, broadly aligns with forward‑looking, inflation‑forecast targeting (Svensson & Woodford, 2005) and Taylor‑rule style prescriptions (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), given evidence of cooling labor markets (“job gains have slowed,” unemployment up) and progress on disinflation. The emphasis on expectations and slack is consistent with the New Keynesian Phillips Curve link between inflation and real marginal cost, while the acknowledgment of uncertainty preserves flexibility to react to shocks (Romer and Romer identification; time‑inconsistency/inflation‑bias concerns). Operationally, continuing balance‑sheet runoff while adjusting policy rates and using IOER/ON RRP/standing repo facilities reflects Goodfriend (2002) on separating implementation tools from the stance. Net tone: dovish but data‑dependent, supportive for growth while maintaining anti‑inflation credibility.
